Dedup-ON golden etalon.
Captured on the tree that shipped post-trim + D4-canonical dedup, AFTER
byte-equal vertex-block sharing landed (blocks fold across pages, so an etalon
captured before it would not match) and AFTER block identity gained the
trim_offset terms. Every frame here sits on its own canvas at its own offset, so
none of the 6 folds shares a block — the region dump is unchanged by that rule,
only the vertex blob length is, which is why the dump and the SHA move apart.
Single-threaded (nt_builder_set_threads(ctx, 1), NT_BUILDER_THREADS=1),
nt_atlas_opts_defaults() unmodified — dedup ON, allowed_transforms = ALL.
Fixture: tests/unit/test_helpers/atlas_dedup_fixture.h, all 10 frames via
atlas_dedup_fixture_add (4 art states on 10 distinct canvas sizes/offsets, so
folding is reachable only after the alpha trim). 10 frames -> 4 placements.
Atlas name "dedup_golden" — the name seeds the texture page resource ids, so
the SHA depends on it; re-capture with any other name will not match.
etalon_dedup_on sha256 6211e908e976764d4b2254cf07c2725ccd3dc0dcbae976908d5215fa3b386a6c
test_atlas_transform_mask::test_golden_byte_identity_dedup_on re-packs the same
fixture, asserts the pack still folds to 4 distinct placements, then asserts
byte-identity against this dump + sha256 pair.
To regenerate after an INTENTIONAL dedup or packer change: run
test_atlas_transform_mask, then take the SHA-256 of
build/tests/tmp/dedup_golden.ntpack and copy
build/tests/tmp/dedup_golden_dump.txt over the dump file (the test also prints
the current dump on divergence). Keep both files LF — pinned in .gitattributes.
